parts.problem_md:
Fig. 1.1 shows an animal cell and a plant cell.

![Diagram comparing labelled animal cell (left) and plant cell (right), showing nucleus, cytoplasm, cell membrane, cell wall, vacuole and other organelles](assets/001-diagram-comparing-labelled-animal-cell-left-and-.png)

**Fig 1.1**

Table 1.1 shows the names and functions of some of the structures of the cells labelled in Fig. 1.1.

| letter in Fig. 1.1 | name of structure | function |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | ...................... | controls the movement of substances into and out of cells |
| **D** | mitochondria | ...................... |
| .......... | vacuole | ...................... |
parts.solution_md:
| letter in Fig. 1.1 | name of structure | function |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | (cell) membrane | controls the movement of substances into and out of cells |
| **D** | mitochondria | (site of aerobic) respiration |
| G | vacuole | support |

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - A: (cell) membrane **[1 mark]**
> - D: (site of aerobic) respiration **[1 mark]**
> - G **[1 mark]**
> - Vacuole: support **[1 mark]**
> 
> Accept storage

> **[exam-tip]**
> Learn each cell structure by pairing it with its single most important function — mitochondria with respiration, vacuole with storage/support — so you can recall them quickly.

**Fig. 1.2**

Use the words from the list to complete Fig. 1.2.

**organ         organ system         tissue**
parts.solution_md:
![Flow chart showing levels of biological organisation: cell to tissue to organ to organ system to organism, linked by downward arrows](assets/003-flow-chart-showing-levels-of-biological-organisa.png)

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - One sequential pair correct **[1 mark]**
> - All three in the correct order **[2 marks]**

parts.problem_md:
The actual length of a phorid fly is 5500 μm long.

What is the magnification of this diagram of a phorid fly?

![Line drawing of a flying insect with wings, antennae and six legs, with a horizontal measurement label underneath showing its length as 35 mm](assets/004-line-drawing-of-a-flying-insect-with-wings-anten.png)
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Magnification = image size ÷ actual size
- Convert units so both are in the same unit: 35 mm = 35 000 μm
- Magnification = 35 000 ÷ 5500 = 6.4

parts.problem_md:
The actual length of a phorid fly is 5.5 mm.

What is the magnification of this diagram of a phorid fly?

![Line drawing of a flying insect with wings, antennae and legs, labelled underneath with a body length measurement of 35 millimetres](assets/005-line-drawing-of-a-flying-insect-with-wings-anten.png)
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- Magnification = image size ÷ actual size
- Magnification = 35 ÷ 5.5 = 6.4

parts.problem_md: What is a type of tissue in a living organism?
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is A**

- Blood is a connective tissue, a group of similar cells working together to perform a shared function

**B** is incorrect because the heart is an organ, not a tissue

**C** is incorrect because plasma is the liquid component of blood, not a tissue in its own right

**D** is incorrect because a plasmid is a small circular DNA molecule found in bacteria, not a tissue

parts.problem_md:
Which label shows the site of aerobic respiration in this diagram of an animal cell?

![Diagram of an irregular animal cell with labelled arrows A to D pointing to cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus and several mitochondria inside](assets/006-diagram-of-an-irregular-animal-cell-with-labelle.png)
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is B**

- The mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration, where most energy is released for the cell

parts.problem_md:
Which label represents a plasmid in this diagram of a bacterium?

![Diagram of a labelled bacterium showing outer flagella, cell wall and membrane, internal cytoplasm, and a central loop of genetic material](assets/007-diagram-of-a-labelled-bacterium-showing-outer-fl.png)
parts.solution_md:
**Final answer:** **The correct answer is C**

- The plasmid is the small circular DNA molecule found in bacteria, separate from the main chromosomal DNA
